title: TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'Ue.type.toLowerCase')
body: ### What happened? trying to edit a query i have just typed in: happens for me on both `grafana-enterprise-10.2.3.linux-arm64.tar.gz` and `grafana-enterprise_10.3.0-64837_64837_darwin_arm64.tar.gz` ### What did you expect to happen? to be able to edit the query ### Did this work before? not sure, just updated grafana from a very old version, started from scratch. ### How do we reproduce it? 1. add a prom query 2. apply, save 3. come back to edit it ### Is the bug inside a dashboard panel? _No response_ ### Environment (with versions)? Grafana: drwxr-xr-x 12 pi pi 4096 Jan 8 21:43 grafana-10.3.0-64837 -rw-r--r-- 1 pi pi 111751536 Dec 19 03:13 grafana-enterprise-10.2.3.linux-arm64.tar.gz -rw-r--r-- 1 pi pi 161598224 Jan 8 21:42 grafana-enterprise_10.3.0-64837_64837_darwin_arm64.tar.gz drwxr-xr-x 12 pi pi 4096 Jan 8 14:41 grafana-v10.2.3 OS: MacOS Browser: Chrome / Safari ### Grafana platform? A downloaded binary ### Datasource(s)? prometheus

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hi @reporter,

Thanks for opening this issue.

Could you please change the default log level to debug mode? 

To do this go to the server where grafana is installed and edit the configuration file (`/etc/grafana/grafana.ini`)

There you will this section;

```
#################################### Logging ##########################
[log]
# Either "console", "file", "syslog". Default is console and  file
# Use space to separate multiple modes, e.g. "console file"
;mode = console file

# Either "debug", "info", "warn", "error", "critical", default is "info"
;level = info
```
Set the parameter level to debug and remove the colon in the beginning i.e.

`level = debug`

Then restart the grafana service and resent the logs once the issue occurs again.


Also, please send us the HAR file by capturing the web session traffic. Here, is a reference [link](https://support.google.com/admanager/answer/10358597?hl=en) as how to capture it using Chrome DevTools.

the problem is gone after changing the following parameters to my prometheus data-source:
- "Default editor" form `Builder` to `Code`
- "Disable metrics lookup" from `off` to `on`

comments.author: participant6
comments.body: @reporter In terms of defensiveness we can add checks everywhere but that will create unnecessary overheat. I'd like to look at this from the API provider and consumer side. And those can be anything. While a consumer uses an API it relies on the other side's contract. The consumer must adjust itself to serve the best out of it. On the other hand API providers must take steps to make sure it will provide the promised data. And if the provider will change something it should deprecate it first and remove it. As a consumer, I don't expect that kind of thing to happen all of a sudden. So instead of the consumer, I would say the provider must be cautious. In this case, Prometheus was strict but that case wasn't covered with a unit test so it just slipped. So when the fix is in place these kinds of cases will be caught and not happen again.
